the study of nuclear structure and reactions with the help of the radioactive beams of the GSI heavy-ion accelerator.
the investigation of the reaction mechanism of the system32S with gold at 373 MeV.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the out-of-plane angular widths of α-particle correlations are sensitive to the out-of-plane momenta of the α-particles at emission and that these momenta depend on theZ of projectile-like heavy ions.
the out-of-plane correlations are not sensitive to the reaction mechanism, and that the α-particles are emitted from a very compact system.
the emission of α-particles is a very sensitive probe for the reaction dynamics of projectilelike fragments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found a very strong correlation of the emission angle of the heavy ion with the emission angle of α-particles in the out-of-plane direction.
the α-particles are emitted from a source with a size of about 1.5 fm, and that the emission process is very fast, i.e., the time of α-particle emission is of the order of a few fm/c.
in the case of the system32S + 197Au at ELA=373 MeV, the α-particle is emitted from a system which is not very hot and which has not yet reached the stage of global equilibration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the angular width of the α-particles is very sensitive to the momentum of α-particle at the time of emission.
α particles can be used as a probe to study the reaction dynamics.
the α-particles are not produced by the decay of excited projectile-like nuclei.
